solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: They're free with their favours, delivering smackers

blocks.note: first meaning: a slang term for promiscuous women
second meaning: people who hand out blows with the open hand

explanation.surface: Generous types handing out kisses, smackers being slang for kisses.
explanation.walkthrough: Smackers reads as kisses, but here it means smacks, and those who deliver them hit with the palm. The first sense is British slang, a vulgar word for a promiscuous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both promiscuous women in coarse British slang and, literally, people who strike with the palm.

clue.text: Constant in trust banco managed to outsource?

indicators.note: in places the constant among the letters that follow, so all join the same fodder
managed suggests letters handled and organised into a new working order

blocks.note: c is the symbol for a constant in mathematics and physics

explanation.surface: A trust bank arranging to farm out its work to another firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Banco is a banking term; the constant joins its letters and those of trust, and all eleven are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To subcontract is to pass work to an outside party, which is exactly what outsourcing means.

clue.text: Sally, maybe perky, judge released

indicators.note: released means let go, so the judge is set free from the word and leaves it

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A cheerful woman called Sally freed by a judge from the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a fairground figure and pub game in Britain, so Sally is an example of an aunty; maybe flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sally is one example of an aunt, via the British fairground target Aunt Sally.

clue.text: Placed Scotch cask to be opened by non-drinker, English

indicators.note: a cask opened by something has that thing put into its middle

blocks.note: a pin is a small cask holding about four and a half gallons
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A Scotch whisky cask placed for a teetotaller to open.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch looks like the whisky but means Scots: the answer is the Scots past participle of put.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitten is the Scots form of put as a past participle, so it means placed in Scottish usage.

clue.text: 'Little' girl in Rome played quietly above hall

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical instruction to play quietly
aula is a hall, from the Latin word

explanation.surface: A small girl in Rome played softly over a hall.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, above puts the first piece on top of the second. The quotation marks show that Little is the meaning of the name, not her size.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman name Paula comes from the Latin paulus, meaning small, so it is the girl named Little.

clue.text: Travelling court to observe around king

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word goes outside the other

explanation.surface: Royal judges on circuit sent out to keep an eye on the king.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyre was a medieval circuit of itinerant justices, a court that moved from county to county.

clue.text: Muslim place housing converted nun

indicators.note: housing means giving a home to, so the place holds the other letters inside
converted means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Muslim household taking in a nun who has changed faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sunnite is an adherent of the Sunni branch of Islam, the larger of its two main traditions.

clue.text: Very powerful writings including one ending in tragedy

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the writings hold the one inside
ending in points only to the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: MSS is the abbreviation for manuscripts

explanation.surface: Powerful writings, one of them ending as a tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Massy is an old word for massive or weighty, so of great bulk and force.

clue.text: Fashionable, but lacking some French — it mustn't be forgotten!

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so some letters are missing from the phrase

blocks.note: de is French for some, as in du pain

explanation.surface: A trendy person whose French is poor, an embarrassing lapse to remember.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the battle cry Remember the Alamo, from the 1836 Texan siege.
explanation.definitionFit: Remember the Alamo was the Texan rallying cry after the 1836 siege, so it is the thing that must not be forgotten.

clue.text: Slices of sourdough inside munched after part of crust

indicators.note: a slice is a small piece cut off the front, so only an opening letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Eating sourdough slices after a bit of the crust.
explanation.walkthrough: Crust looks like bread, but it is the Earth's crust; after belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sima is the lower layer of the Earth's crust, rich in silica and magnesium, under the continents and ocean floor.

clue.text: Sailors in service as once watched which way they rowed?

indicators.note: in places the sailors inside the old word for service

blocks.note: steed is an old spelling of stead, which once meant service or help

explanation.surface: Sailors in service long ago, keeping an eye on the direction of their rowing.
explanation.walkthrough: Stern was once a verb meaning to steer, so sterned is an old word for steered; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern as an obsolete verb meant to steer, and someone steering a rowing boat keeps watch on its course.

clue.text: When the sun last went down the view includes water bird

definitions.text: When the sun last went down

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so the view surrounds the bird

blocks.note: ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: At sunset, a bird on the water appears in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesternight is an old word for last night, the night after the most recent sunset.

clue.text: Bird you probably won't see appearing regularly in the urinal

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A bird nobody expects to spot in the gents' urinal.
explanation.definitionFit: The huia was a New Zealand wattlebird, extinct since the early twentieth century, so nobody is likely to see one.

clue.text: Lady's maid getting money that's very little worked better

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so the following word is reformed

blocks.note: a sou was a French coin of tiny value

explanation.surface: A maid on tiny wages who works harder.
explanation.definitionFit: A soubrette is a pert lady's maid in comedy, and by extension any such coquettish female role.

clue.text: One akin to goosefoot? It's found amid the alien corn

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: blé is the French for corn, so foreign corn

explanation.surface: A weed growing among the foreign corn, echoing Keats's Ruth amid the alien corn.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is from Keats's Ode to a Nightingale; alien here means foreign-language, so the corn is the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Blite is a name for several plants of the goosefoot family, such as strawberry blite.

clue.text: Wild carnivore adapting to inn grub

indicators.note: adapting means altering to suit, so the letters are changed in order

explanation.surface: A wild animal getting used to pub food.
explanation.definitionFit: The binturong, or bearcat, is a Southeast Asian civet that eats meat as well as fruit.

clue.text: Bully once let off after unkind deed

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the word's letters are out of order

blocks.note: a cut is an unkind act, a snub

explanation.surface: A bully of old let off after a cruel act.
explanation.walkthrough: After puts the rearranged word behind the unkind deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuttle is an obsolete word for a bully or cutpurse-style swaggerer, as in Shakespeare's Henry IV.

clue.text: Mum's appearing in funny turns, anything but slick, …

indicators.note: appearing in means showing up inside, so one piece goes within the other
funny means odd, so the letters of the word that follows are put in an odd order

blocks.note: its letters rearranged around the mother

explanation.surface: Mum doing comic turns on stage, hardly polished.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the next clue for surface only. Mum's is Mum is.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsmart lacks polish or style, so it is far from slick.

clue.text: Medicinal bark for each age, including one

indicators.note: including means containing, so the age holds the one inside

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A medicinal bark taken for each age, one included.
explanation.definitionFit: Pereira bark comes from a Brazilian tree and was once used as a tonic and febrifuge in medicine.

clue.text: Discussion group remains disorganized

indicators.note: disorganized means in disarray, so the letters are out of order

explanation.surface: A discussion group that is still in a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small class or meeting where a group discusses a subject.

clue.text: … Live, including muggins, hackneyed stuff, old hat

indicators.note: including means containing, so the verb holds the other pieces inside

blocks.note: to be is to live, to exist
muggins is a fool, used jokingly for oneself, so I

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue, living with tired clichés is old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Old hat looks like the idiom for stale, but it is literal: a hat of earlier times.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicorne is a two-cornered hat of the Napoleonic era, so an old style of headwear.

clue.text: Reactionary so-and-so from Norway earned terribly old German money?

indicators.note: terribly means very badly, so the word's letters are badly arranged

blocks.note: N is the international code for Norway
the thaler was a silver coin of the German states

explanation.surface: A backward Norwegian who made a killing in old German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neanderthaler is literally a Neanderthal man, and figuratively a boorish person with primitive, reactionary views.

clue.text: Proud as before, old copper is on top of the facts (mostly)

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: the as was a Roman copper coin

explanation.surface: A smug old policeman who has the facts nearly in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman, but it is the Roman coin. As before marks the definition as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrut is an archaic word for strutting or swelling out, the bearing of someone puffed up with pride.

clue.text: Salamis probably featured this meatier recipe, one cut

indicators.note: cut means removed, so the single letter is taken away
probably admits doubt about the order, so the letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A recipe for a meatier salami, misdirecting as cured sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: Salamis is the Greek island where the Athenian fleet beat the Persians in 480 BC, not a plural of salami. The definition is the whole clue's opening: probably does double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The trireme, a galley with three banks of oars, was the warship used at the naval battle of Salamis.

clue.text: Do Americans use mallets for this? (Question digested by rake)

definitions.text: Do Americans use mallets for this?

indicators.note: something digested by another is taken inside it

blocks.note: a roué is a rake, a debauched man

explanation.surface: Asking whether Americans use mallets, with an aside about a question swallowed by a garden rake.
explanation.walkthrough: Rake looks like the garden tool but is a libertine.
explanation.definitionFit: Roque is an American form of croquet played on a hard court, using mallets to hit balls through hoops.

clue.text: Zemindar's fitted out men with this tailor

indicators.note: out means removed, so the men are taken away
fitted means altered to fit, so the remaining letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An Indian landowner's men are fitted out with clothes by this tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: A zemindar was a landholder in British India, which keeps the scene in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Darzi is the Hindi and Urdu word for a tailor, used in Anglo-Indian English.

clue.text: Herd maybe accepts old dialect that's spread

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the herd holds the letter inside

blocks.note: kine is an old plural of cow, so a herd

explanation.surface: A herd taking on an old dialect that has spread widely.
explanation.definitionFit: Koine is the common Greek spoken across the Hellenistic world, and any lingua franca that spreads among peoples.

clue.text: Poultries straying (apart from pair inside) lay away from brood?

indicators.note: apart from means except, so a pair of interior letters is excluded
straying means wandering from place, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: Wandering hens laying their eggs away from the brood.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair removed is the U and L in the middle of the word. Lay away looks like a hen laying out of the nest, but means store.
explanation.definitionFit: To reposit is to put something away in store; the question mark nods to a hen laying eggs elsewhere.

clue.text: Attempt taking in old information from the US

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the attempt surrounds the letter

blocks.note: to have a pop is to have an attempt

explanation.surface: An effort to pull in old data from America.
explanation.definitionFit: Poop is American slang for inside information or the latest news.

clue.text: Courses over I'll come to sudden enlightenment

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: rotas are rosters, courses of duty in turn

explanation.surface: After the courses I'll finally see the light.
explanation.definitionFit: Satori is the Zen Buddhist term for a sudden flash of spiritual awakening.

clue.text: Sound unit, as it's said, worked with machine?

indicators.note: as it's said points to speech, the word as heard rather than as spelt

blocks.note: a sone is a unit of perceived loudness

explanation.surface: A unit of sound, apparently, produced by a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: stitching can be done by hand too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewn is the past participle of sew, and fabric worked on a sewing machine has been sewn.

clue.text: Completely covering cooking tin, wrong

indicators.note: cooking means preparing by mixing, so the letters of the next word are stirred

explanation.surface: Covering a cooking tin entirely is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Interring means burying, putting earth over a body so that it is wholly covered.

clue.text: Whip applied round centre of bum — it's behind the saddle

indicators.note: applied round means wrapped about, so the whip encloses the letter
centre points to the middle letter of the following word

blocks.note: a crop is a riding whip

explanation.surface: A riding crop applied to a horse's backside, which lies behind the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A croup is the rump of a horse, the hindquarters behind where the saddle sits.

clue.text: Native of New Mexico maybe, last character to attend advanced instruction

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A New Mexican going off to college at the last moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zuni are a Pueblo people of western New Mexico; maybe signals the Zuni is one example of a native.

clue.text: Got the measure of little 'un bottling potential energy

indicators.note: bottling means holding inside, so the little one encloses the energy

blocks.note: a tad is a small child, a little one
PE is the standard abbreviation in physics

explanation.surface: Sizing up a small child bursting with untapped energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Got the measure of looks like understood, but here it means measured with a tape.
explanation.definitionFit: To tape something is to measure it with a tape measure, so taped means measured.

clue.text: Energy to preserve? Torn about reverse of that, rarely holding back

indicators.note: reverse of means backwards, so the preceding pieces are read from the end
about means surrounding, so the torn word goes round the other

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy
to tin is to preserve food in a can

explanation.surface: Energy needed to preserve something torn, with resistance rarely shown.
explanation.walkthrough: Rarely is part of the definition, flagging a rare word, not a selection signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Renitent is a rare word for resisting pressure or reluctant, so it describes someone holding back.
